chunks: Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There are three for whom their deeds will not be raised: an absconder slave, and a woman whose husband is angered upon her, and the one who drags his trousers in arrogance.

key_terms.الْمُسْبِلُ: The one who drags their lower garment
key_terms.زَوْجُهَا عَلَيْهَا سَاخِطٌ: A woman whose husband is angered upon her
key_terms.عَبْدٌ آبِقٌ: An absconder slave who runs away from their master

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of people whose deeds are not accepted in Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight specific conditions that nullify the spiritual reward of good deeds, emphasizing the interplay between individual piety and social or domestic harmony. The inclusion of the 'wife upon whom her husband is angry' underscores the Shia emphasis on marital rights and the gravity of discord within the family unit as a barrier to divine acceptance. Furthermore, linking the slave's escape and the arrogant dragger of garments illustrates how both servitude and pride can obstruct spiritual elevation if not rectified.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Musa Bin Bakr, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘There are three for whom deeds would not be raised, ever – An absconder (slave), and a woman whose husband is angered upon her, and the one who drags his trousers for pomp’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn al-Hakam from has narrated from Musa ibn Bakr who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The good deeds of three kinds of people cannot rise up. One is a runaway slave, a woman whose husband is not happy with her and one who drags his gown on the ground out of pride.’”
